text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

Australian singer NELLIE MELBA was born in 1861. She was originally named HELEN PORTER MITCHELL. DAME NELLIE was the leading singer of her time and one of Australia's first international stars. She retired from the stage and came back so many times, it gave rise to the saying "More comebacks than MELBA".

North Vietnamese leader HO CHI MINH was born in 1890. He was educated in Paris, and became a Communist. He returned to his homeland, gained leadership in the North and was leader during the Vietnam War. He died before the North won the war.
American black muslim leader MALCOLM X was born in 1926.
Australian fashion designer CARLA ZAMPATTI was born in 1940.
British rock star PETE TOWNSHEND was born in 1945. He gained fame through the band 'The Who', and the rock musical 'Tommy'.
Australian rock star JAMES REYNE was born in 1957. He became famous through the band 'Australian Crawl' before launching a solo career.
** EVENTS **
1536 : ANNE BOLEYN was executed by her husband HENRY THE

8TH. She was sentenced to death for treason after her first son was stillborn. The reality was that HENRY had become infatuated with ANNE's Lady-in-waiting JANE SEYMOUR. HENRY had created the Church of England after the Pope originally wouldn't let him marry ANNE.
1643 : The towns of Connecticut, Plymouth and New Haven
formed a Confederation of the United Colonies of New England as protection in the wars with the Indians.
1795 : JAMES BOSWELL, Scottish diarist and biographer and
companion to Dr SAMUEL JOHNSON, died. His famous biography "Life of Johnson" was published in 1791.
1898 : WILLIAM EWART GLADSTONE, British statesman and
prime minister four times, died. An advocate of social and political reform, he tried without success to bring home rule to Ireland.
1900 : Tonga was annexed by Britain.
1906: The 12-mile Simplon rail tunnel between
Switzerland and Italy was officially opened.
1915 : One of Australia's most famous Anzacs was killed
by a sniper's bullet. JOHN SIMPSON KIRKPATRICK rescued dozens of wounded soldiers, carrying them from the battlefield on his donkey.
1930 : White women were given the vote in South Africa.
1935 : T.E. LAWRENCE died five days after being seriously
injured in a motorcycle accident. He became famous during the First World War for rallying the nomadic Arab tribes to the Allied cause. He gained the name 'LAWRENCE OF ARABIA'.
1953 : The 100,000th Holden rolled off the assembly line
after four and a half years of production in Melbourne.
1978 : In Melbourne, more than 60,000 people lined the
streets for Sir ROBERT MENZIES' funeral.
1980 : 15 people were killed when Mt ST. HELENS erupted
in the United States. The volcano hadn't erupted for more than 130 years, and didn't give any warning of the disaster.
1991 : HELEN SHARMAN became the first Briton in space,
when she blasted off on board a Russian spacecraft.
1993 : A Colombian jetliner crashed outside the city of
Medellin. 132 people were killed. The crash was later blamed on a bomb planted by a local drug cartel to kill a number of officials who were on the plane.
1994 : Former Prime Minister MALCOLM FRASER announced
that he believed then Shadow Treasurer ALEXANDER DOWNER should be leading the Liberal Party instead of JOHN HEWSON.
1994 : MARK TAYLOR was selected to replace ALLAN BORDER
as Australian cricket captain.
1994 : Malawi's aged, autocratic President KAMUZU BANDA
conceded victory to opposition leader BAKILI MULUZI after more than 30 years of iron-fisted rule.
1994 : JACQUELINE KENNEDY ONASSIS, queen of a long-lost

American Camelot and a world-wide symbol of jet-set glamour, died. In 1953, she married the future President JOHN F. KENNEDY and in 1968, five years after his assassination, she married shipping tycoon ARISTOTLE ONASSIS.
